s: Under the Census 2011 framework, Scheduled Castes were notified in how many States and Union Territories, covering approximately how many groups?
x: Scheduled Castes were notified in 31 States and Union Territories, covering 1,241 groups.
tq: Use the paired numerical figures together to avoid confusing the number of jurisdictions with the number of groups.
sec: States/UTs with no notified SC population - list and reasons

s: Which one of the following correctly explains why certain north-eastern and island territories have no notified Scheduled Caste population?
o: They have only migrant populations and no permanent inhabitants.
They were excluded because Article 341 does not apply to any Union Territory.
Their populations are exclusively urban and therefore outside the Census classification.
Their populations are overwhelmingly tribal, whereas Scheduled Caste status is historically associated with untouchability in the Hindu caste order.
x: The populations concerned are overwhelmingly tribal. Scheduled Caste identification is linked to untouchability in the Hindu caste order, while Scheduled Tribes are identified by tribal characteristics.
tq: Distinguish the basis of Scheduled Caste identification from the tribal basis of Scheduled Tribe identification.
sec: States/UTs with no notified SC population - list and reasons

s:
With reference to the constitutional position of Arunachal Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. The 83rd Constitutional Amendment was enacted in 2000.
2. It removed the need for reservation of Scheduled Caste seats in panchayats of Arunachal Pradesh.
3. The provision was related to the wholly tribal character of the State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The 83rd Amendment of 2000 removed the need for Scheduled Caste reservation in Arunachal Pradesh panchayats because the State is wholly tribal.
tq: Check whether the amendment, year and constitutional rationale form a single consistent set.
sec: States/UTs with no notified SC population - list and reasons

s:
Scheduled Caste status under the relevant legal framework is available to which of the following religious communities?
1. Hindus
2. Sikhs
3. Buddhists
4. Jains
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Scheduled Caste status is available to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists. Sikhs were added in 1956 and Buddhists in 1990; Jains are not included in this list.
tq: Test the confusable religious categories by identifying the two communities added subsequently.
sec: States/UTs with no notified SC population - list and reasons

s: Which State had the highest proportion of Scheduled Castes in its population according to Census 2011?
x: Punjab had the highest Scheduled Caste share at about 31.9%, followed by Himachal Pradesh at 25.2% and West Bengal at 23.5%.
tq: Separate percentage share from absolute population size; the largest share need not be in the most populous State.
sec: States with highest SC share vs highest absolute SC population

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Scheduled Caste share of the population in Census 2011:
1. Punjab recorded about 31.9 percent.
2. Himachal Pradesh recorded about 25.2 percent.
3. West Bengal recorded about 23.5 percent.
4. Mizoram recorded about 10.1 percent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and West Bengal recorded approximately 31.9%, 25.2% and 23.5%, respectively. Mizoram had only about 0.1%, not 10.1%.
tq: Watch the decimal-place trap in percentage figures and distinguish high shares from negligible shares.
sec: States with highest SC share vs highest absolute SC population

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Himachal Pradesh — about 31.9% Scheduled Caste share
x: Mizoram had the lowest Scheduled Caste share among States with Scheduled Castes, at about 0.1%. Meghalaya followed with about 0.6%; Punjab and Himachal Pradesh had much higher shares.
tq: Start with the sure State–percentage pair and reject reversed or shifted percentages.
sec: States with highest SC share vs highest absolute SC population

s: The Scheduled Caste population of Andhra Pradesh in Census 2011 was approximately what percentage of India’s total Scheduled Caste population?
x: Andhra Pradesh had about 84.69 lakh Scheduled Castes, constituting approximately 4.21% of India’s Scheduled Caste population.
tq: Distinguish the State’s share of India’s Scheduled Caste population from its share within the State population.
sec: States with highest SC share vs highest absolute SC population

s: According to Census 2011, the Scheduled Caste population of India was approximately:
x: India’s Scheduled Caste population was approximately 20.14 crore, or 16.6% of the total population, in Census 2011.
tq: Keep the absolute count and percentage together; the nearby 12.6% and 18.5% figures refer to urban and rural population shares.
sec: SC population Census 2011 - national share and count

s: The approximate sex ratio of the Scheduled Caste population in India, calculated from the Census 2011 figures, was:
x: The Scheduled Caste population included about 1,035.35 lakh males and 978.43 lakh females, giving an approximate sex ratio of 945 females per 1,000 males.
tq: Use the male–female figures to distinguish the calculated ratio from either component figure.
sec: SC population Census 2011 - national share and count

s: The Scheduled Caste population of Andhra Pradesh increased from approximately 32.73 lakh in 1971 to what figure in 2011?
x: The Scheduled Caste population of Andhra Pradesh rose from 32.73 lakh in 1971 to 84.69 lakh in 2011.
tq: Use the first and last values in the time sequence before considering the distractors.
sec: SC population Census 2011 - national share and count

s: Which district recorded the highest Scheduled Caste share in India according to the cited district-level figures?
x: Koch Bihar district of West Bengal recorded the highest Scheduled Caste share, at about 50%. Shahid Bhagat Singh Nagar followed with a share above 40%.
tq: Distinguish the leading district from the district occupying the next position.
sec: District-level concentration - highest SC share districts

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Shahid Bhagat Singh Nagar — about 20% Scheduled Caste share
Koch Bihar — about 50% Scheduled Caste share
x: Shahid Bhagat Singh Nagar had a Scheduled Caste share above 40%, not about 20%. Koch Bihar is in West Bengal and had a share of about 50%.
tq: Find the altered percentage in an otherwise correctly matched district–State pair.
sec: District-level concentration - highest SC share districts

s: Scheduled Castes are particularly concentrated in which of the following geographical settings?
o: Isolated island territories and north-eastern hill districts
High Himalayan slopes and dense forest interiors only
Fertile alluvial plains and coastal delta regions
Arid deserts and cold trans-Himalayan valleys
x: Scheduled Castes are relatively dense in fertile alluvial plains such as Punjab, the Ganga plain, West Bengal and coastal deltas, where settled farming historically used landless labour.
tq: Link the population pattern to the geographical and occupational setting rather than selecting a broad physical region at random.
sec: District-level concentration - highest SC share districts

s: Under Article 341(1) of the Constitution, who specifies the Scheduled Castes for each State or Union Territory by public notification?
o: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes
The Governor, after consulting the President
The President, after consulting the Governor concerned
x: Article 341(1) empowers the President, after consultation with the Governor, to specify Scheduled Castes for each State or Union Territory by public notification.
tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to separate the President’s notification power from Parliament’s amendment power.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Article 341 notification, Article 46, reserved constituencies

s:
Consider the following statements about Article 341:
1. The President specifies Scheduled Castes for a State or Union Territory by public notification.
2. Parliament alone can include or exclude a group from the notified list by law.
3. A State Government may unilaterally alter the notified list through an executive order.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A State Government cannot unilaterally alter the notified list; inclusion or exclusion is possible only through a law made by Parliament under Article 341(2).
tq: Use the authority trap by separating constitutional notification from the power to amend the list.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Article 341 notification, Article 46, reserved constituencies

s: The first list of Scheduled Castes was issued through the:
x: The first list was issued through the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950. The term ‘Scheduled Castes’ itself had appeared earlier in the Government of India Act, 1935.
tq: Separate the origin of the term from the constitutional instrument that issued the first list.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Article 341 notification, Article 46, reserved constituencies

s: Which one of the following is the principal directive contained in Article 46?
o: To notify Scheduled Castes for each State and Union Territory
To abolish untouchability through criminal law alone
To promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, especially SCs and STs, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation
To reserve all public offices exclusively for SCs and STs
x: Article 46, a Directive Principle of State Policy, directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, especially SCs and STs, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation.
tq: Match the Article with its precise function instead of confusing it with notification, abolition or reservation provisions.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Article 341 notification, Article 46, reserved constituencies

s: Articles 330 and 332 provide for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the:
o: Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies
Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils
Lok Sabha and Gram Sabhas only
x: Articles 330 and 332 provide reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, respectively.
tq: Distinguish parliamentary and State Assembly reservation provisions from local-body and upper-house provisions.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Article 341 notification, Article 46, reserved constituencies

s: The number of reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha rose from 79 and 41 respectively to what figures after the 2001-Census delimitation?
x: The reserved Lok Sabha seats increased from 79 for Scheduled Castes and 41 for Scheduled Tribes to 84 and 47, respectively, after the 2001-Census delimitation.
tq: Treat the paired figures as two separate columns and avoid reversing the SC and ST numbers.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Article 341 notification, Article 46, reserved constituencies

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 334 — National Commission for Scheduled Castes
Article 341 — Directive Principle concerning weaker sections
x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability. Article 338 concerns the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, Article 334 relates to the duration of reservation, and Article 341 concerns specification of Scheduled Castes.
tq: Use the Article-number trap by matching each provision with its exact constitutional subject.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Article 341 notification, Article 46, reserved constituencies

s: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2019 extended reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in legislatures up to:
x: The 104th Amendment extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in legislatures up to 2030.
tq: Identify the amendment-year pair first and then retain the specific extension year.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Article 341 notification, Article 46, reserved constituencies

s: Which body is associated with Article 338?
x: Article 338 provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.
tq: Avoid the neighbouring constitutional-body trap by matching the Article with the exact commission.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Article 341 notification, Article 46, reserved constituencies

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the rural–urban distribution of Scheduled Castes in 2011:
1. About 76% of Scheduled Castes lived in rural areas.
2. About 24% lived in urban areas.
3. Scheduled Castes constituted about 18.5% of India’s rural population.
4. Scheduled Castes constituted about 12.6% of India’s urban population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct. In 2011, approximately 76% of Scheduled Castes lived in rural areas and 24% in urban areas; their shares were about 18.5% of the rural population and 12.6% of the urban population.
tq: Keep the distribution percentages separate from the SC share within rural and urban populations.
sec: Rural-urban distribution of SCs

s: Which statement correctly compares the rural concentration of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
o: Scheduled Castes are urban-dominant, whereas Scheduled Tribes are rural-minority groups.
Scheduled Castes are more rural than Scheduled Tribes, with 89.97% of STs living in urban areas.
Scheduled Tribes are more rural than Scheduled Castes, with about 89.97% of STs living in rural areas.
Both groups have exactly the same rural distribution.
x: Scheduled Tribes are even more rural than Scheduled Castes; about 89.97% of the ST population lived in rural areas.
tq: Check the direction of comparison and the meaning of the percentage before selecting the option.
sec: Rural-urban distribution of SCs

s: Which one of the following correctly states the literacy position of Scheduled Castes in comparison with the national average?
o: SC literacy was about 66.1%, compared with a national average of about 73–74%.
SC literacy exceeded the national average by about 10 percentage points.
SC literacy was about 50%, equal to the national average.
SC literacy was about 73–74%, compared with a national average of about 66.1%.
x: Scheduled Caste literacy was reported at about 66.1%, lower than the national average of approximately 73–74%. Some compilations cite 66.4%, but the cited figure here is 66.1%.
tq: Use the direction of the comparison and beware of reversing the group figure with the national figure.
sec: Literacy and occupational profile of SCs vs national average

s:
With reference to the cited 2017–18 and 2018 indicators, consider the following statements:
1. Scheduled Caste unemployment was 5.5%, compared with 5% nationally.
2. Scheduled Caste infant mortality was 44, compared with 32 nationally.
3. Scheduled Caste unemployment was lower than the national rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Scheduled Caste unemployment was 5.5% against 5% nationally, while SC infant mortality was 44 against 32; therefore statement 3 is false.
tq: Detect the reversed comparison in the third statement after verifying the two numerical pairs.
sec: Literacy and occupational profile of SCs vs national average

s: Which occupational pattern is most closely associated with the Scheduled Caste population?
o: Predominantly large landowners and industrial entrepreneurs
Mostly marginal farmers and landless agricultural labourers
Mainly plantation owners and commercial bankers
x: Scheduled Castes are predominantly associated with marginal farming and landless agricultural labour. Upper castes have historically been more closely linked with land ownership.
tq: Link occupational structure with land ownership and avoid the absolute word ‘exclusively’.
sec: Literacy and occupational profile of SCs vs national average

s:
Arrange the following social groups in descending order of their school enrolment shares:
A. OBC
B. Scheduled Tribe
C. General
D. Scheduled Caste
Select the correct sequence.
x: The enrolment shares were OBC 49%, General 27%, Scheduled Caste 17% and Scheduled Tribe 10%, giving the order A, C, D, B.
tq: Arrange the figures from highest to lowest, using the extreme values first.
sec: Literacy and occupational profile of SCs vs national average

s: Which State is noted for having one of the highest Scheduled Caste enrolment shares?
x: Punjab was noted as having one of the highest Scheduled Caste enrolment shares.
tq: Use the State-specific distinction in the enrolment data rather than the State’s overall SC share alone.
sec: Literacy and occupational profile of SCs vs national average

s: Scheduled Castes constituted approximately what proportion of district judges according to the cited figure?
x: Scheduled Castes constituted approximately 14% of district judges in the cited figure.
tq: Separate representation in a professional category from population-share figures such as 14%, 16.6% and 31.9%.
sec: Literacy and occupational profile of SCs vs national average

s: Census 2027 is expected to be significant because it will:
o: replace the population Census with a socio-economic survey
enumerate only Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes for the first time after independence
exclude caste information from the population enumeration
enumerate all castes for the first time in independent India, rather than only SCs and STs
x: Census 2027 is described as the first enumeration of all castes in independent India, rather than an enumeration limited to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
tq: Watch the scope trap between ‘all castes’ and ‘only SCs/STs’.
sec: Universal angles

s: Why are southern States apprehensive about a post-2026 delimitation exercise?
o: They oppose the constitutional recognition of Scheduled Castes.
They fear that SC and ST reservation will be abolished completely.
They fear losing seats when SC/ST reserved seats are re-fixed on the basis of new Census shares.
They expect all rural constituencies to become urban constituencies.
x: A post-2026 delimitation may re-fix Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe reserved seats according to new Census shares, creating a fear of seat loss among southern States.
tq: Identify the institutional cause of the concern instead of treating it as opposition to reservation itself.
sec: Universal angles

s: Who reviewed Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe schemes in Nellore in the cited Andhra Pradesh-related development?
o: K. S. Jawahar, Chairman of the State SC Commission
The Governor of Andhra Pradesh acting under Article 341
The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
x: K. S. Jawahar, Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State SC Commission, reviewed SC/ST schemes in Nellore.
tq: Match the person, office and activity precisely; do not substitute a constitutional authority with a State commission.
sec: Universal angles
